COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C-482 Petition No. 813 of 2021
Hon 'ble N.S.Dh an ik , J.
 The matter is heard through Video
Conferencing.
 Mr. T.P.S.Takuli, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
 Mr. J.S.Virk, Deputy Advocate General for
the State.
 Mr. Akhil Kumar Sah, Advocate for the
private respondent.
 Vide judgment and order dated 13.05.2013,
passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Nainital, District Nainital, the applicant has been
convicted for the offence under Section 138 of the
N.I. Act and sentenced to undergo simple
imprisonment for three months and to pay a fine of
Rs. 5000/-. The applicant preferred an appeal
against the order dated 13.05.2013, bearing appeal
no. 76 of 2013, which was dismissed by the
appellate court on 25.09.2014.
 This C-482 Petition has been moved along
with the compounding application to quash the said
judgment and order. The same is shown as
defective. Learned counsel for the petitioner
undertakes to cure the defects forthwith.
Compounding application is duly supported by the
affidavits of convict-applicant and the
complainant-respondent no.2. It has been stated in
the compounding application that parties have
amicably settled their dispute and the complainant
does not have any objection if the offence is
compounded and impugned judgment is quashed.
Complainant also stated that he has received the
amount in question. Convict applicant and the
complainant, are duly identified by their respective
Counsels.
 Learned State counsel admitted that the

offence is compoundable and does not oppose the
compounding application.
 Reliance has been placed on the verdict of
Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Damodar S.
Prabhu v. Sayed Babalal H., AIR 2010 SC 1907,
and a judgment of Gujarat High Court rendered in
Rajesh Madhusudan Rajyaguru & Anr. V. State of
Gujarat, 2020 (2) Crimes (HC) 719, wherein it has
been held that the parties, in reference to offence
under Section 138 N.I. Act read with Section 147
of the Act are at liberty to compound the matter at
any stage and person affected can pray to court that
accused, on compounding of offence may be
released by invoking jurisdiction of this Court
under Section 482 Cr.P.C. read with Article 226 of
the Constitution of India.
 Convict-applicant is ready to deposit 15 per
cent of the cheque amount as per the dictum of
Hon'ble Apex Court in Damodar S. Prabhu case
(supra).
 Considering the facts and circumstances of
the case and the legal proposition discussed above,
the compounding application is allowed and the
offence is compounded and the impugned
judgment and the said orders dated 13.05.2013 and
25.09.2014 are hereby quashed and set aside.
Conviction of the applicant is quashed. Applicant is
in jail. She is directed to be released forthwith, if
not convicted in any other case. However, it is
made clear that this order is subject to deposition of
15 per cent of the cheque amount within 15 days
from today with the Uttarakhand State Legal
Services Authority, failing which this order shall be
deemed to have been withdrawn and shall be
treated as not est. Further, the certified copy of this
order would be provided only after defects are
cleared.
 Present C-482 petition stands disposed of.

( N. S. Dh an ik , J.)
 07.05.2021
Kaushal
